answer: Rhythm-Priced Identity Admission: each identity must submit its first N actions as a paced stream, with inter-arrival times drawn from a shared schedule. Agents that fall outside the population's timing envelope on any thread get throttled or dropped. An opal watermark embedded in the admission payload ties each stream to its claimed arrival slot. Attackers must pay per-identity latency costs, running slow, coordinated sock-puppet fleets that each hold a distinct vertex in the schedule rather than bursting one.
